blocks.text: Alcohols can be made from alkenes, halogenoalkanes, carbonyl compounds, carboxylic acids and esters.

items: From alkenes with steam: hot steam reacts with an alkene, with concentrated phosphoric acid as catalyst, by electrophilic addition: CH2=CH2 + H2O(g) -> CH3CH2OH (H3PO4, heat).
From alkenes with cold dilute KMnO4: this mild oxidising agent gives a diol: CH2=CH2 + H2O + [O] -> HOCH2CH2OH (ethane-1,2-diol).
From halogenoalkanes: heating with aqueous NaOH substitutes -OH for the halogen: CH3CH2Br + NaOH -> CH3CH2OH + NaBr.

By reducing aldehydes and ketones with NaBH4 or LiAlH4: aldehydes give primary alcohols, e.g. CH3CHO + 2[H] -> CH3CH2OH; ketones give secondary alcohols, e.g. CH3COCH3 + 2[H] -> CH3CH(OH)CH3 (propan-2-ol).
By reducing carboxylic acids with LiAlH4, giving primary alcohols: CH3COOH + 4[H] -> CH3CH2OH + H2O.
By hydrolysing esters: heating with dilute acid or alkali gives a carboxylic acid and an alcohol: CH3COOCH2CH3 + H2O <=> CH3COOH + CH3CH2OH (H+).

blocks.alt: Six boxes with arrows to 'alcohol': ethene + steam with H3PO4 gives ethanol; ethene + water + [O] with cold dilute KMnO4 gives ethane-1,2-diol; bromoethane + NaOH(aq) gives ethanol; ethanal + 2[H] (NaBH4 or LiAlH4) gives a primary alcohol; propanone + 2[H] gives a secondary alcohol; ethanoic acid + 4[H] (LiAlH4) gives ethanol + water. A line adds ester hydrolysis.
blocks.caption: Ways of making alcohols (original summary of the book's methods).
blocks.long_description: Alcohols come from addition to alkenes, substitution of halogenoalkanes, reduction of carbonyl compounds and acids, and hydrolysis of esters. In each case the product carries an -OH group where the starting compound had a double bond, a halogen, a C=O group or an ester link.

blocks.prompt: Which reducing agent can reduce a carboxylic acid to an alcohol, and what type of alcohol forms?
blocks.explanation: LiAlH4; a primary alcohol (e.g. ethanoic acid gives ethanol).

items: Alkene + steam (H3PO4) -> alcohol; alkene + cold dilute KMnO4 -> diol.
RX + NaOH(aq) -> ROH; aldehyde -> 1 alcohol, ketone -> 2 alcohol (NaBH4/LiAlH4); acid -> 1 alcohol (LiAlH4).
